notes: The three 'one for X' pairs are split per token, each dative carrying its own 'for' under rule 21; rule 103's repeated-function-word clause is not in play, no Greek preposition governing the series.
'for us' is kept with the accusative ἡμᾶς as the English marker of the infinitive's subject; placing 'for' on εἶναι remains defensible, but rule 27 keeps the helper with the word it introduces.
The juncture 'and' after 'answered' goes to εἶπεν, the verb it introduces (rule 88), and δέ takes the verse-initial 'And'.
τῷ before Ἰησοῦ is unrepresented and the case preposition 'unto' stays with the name (rules 21, 23).
